rv.q: Webster's captivating production was first staged at Sheffield Crucible in 2019, its original West End transfer scuppered by lockdown.
Max Webster's production of Life Of Pi has weathered better; and is now, quite simply, a wonder to behold.
But for theatregoers looking for a new dimension in puppetry and storytelling, this tale of fur and fortitude is just amazing.
As a work of living, breathing theatre it is, at its best, utterly transcendent.
Life of Pi is a magic eye trick that never lets you look too long at its flaws.
These animals and effects are a wonder to behold and become the real stars of this show.
"Life of Pi" is fantastical, and director Max Webster’s extraordinary West End production is fantastic.
This amazing technical achievement should be seen, and marvelled at, by anyone with an interest in making stage scenery.
Otherwise, this is a gorgeous staging by adaptor Lolita Chakrabarti and director Max Webster: vivid, witty, poignant and wondrous.

Life of Pi is a sumptuous, visual treat for the senses, a remarkably vivid recreation of a classic novel, and an effective reminder that sometimes the stories we tell ourselves are stronger than the truth.
If you want theatrical magic, Life of Pi is the show for you.
The technical wizardry alone is worth the ticket price.
A lack of depth and character development meant that individuals did not stay with me as I left.
This is a magical show that deals with grief and belief in a way that is truly unique.
Life of Pi really is one of the greatest plays the West End has seen in a long time and one of the theatre highlights of the year.

cn.t: Critics hail this adaptation as a visual triumph, with stunning puppetry and technical wizardry that rivals War Horse. While some find it emotionally distant, most praise its dazzling spectacle and imaginative staging of the "unstageable" novel.
